title: Create the Next.js and TypeScript application shell

input.requestedOutcome: Create and publish an isolated Next.js App Router shell for the modernization work.
acceptanceCriteria: The shell runs locally and in CI.
The shell uses Next.js App Router and strict TypeScript.
The shell provides navigation, environment configuration, linting, unit-test setup, and a health page.
The shell does not replace production modules or change persistence behavior.
constraints: Do not modify the legacy production module, SQL, persistence mappings, existing API behavior, root/shared configuration, or SYSTEM_MAP.md.
Do not transition Jira or merge the PR.
Publish a pull request targeting main without force-pushing.
assumptions: No apps/web shell existed on origin/main.
Existing root deployment remains the production application.
CI integration changes are outside this task's permitted scope.

output.summary: Added an isolated, audited Next.js 16 App Router shell with strict TypeScript, shared navigation, static health page, public environment defaults, ESLint, Vitest, and repeatable package scripts without touching legacy behavior.

filesChanged.purpose: Self-contained Next.js application shell, configuration, source, tests, documentation, and lockfile.

behaviorChanges.after: A strict TypeScript Next.js App Router shell is available under apps/web.
The shell provides shared navigation plus static / and /health pages.

behaviorChanges.before: Legacy persistence behavior was active only in the existing application.
behaviorChanges.after: Unchanged; the shell has no legacy imports, API requests, database access, or write paths.

added: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME and NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV optional public display variables
apps/web package scripts: dev, build, start, typecheck, lint, test

details: No database, schema, migration, mapper, API, localStorage, or legacy production module was changed.
The isolated shell has no persistence or write path.

verification.evidence: ESLint completed successfully with Next core-web-vitals rules.
Vitest 3.2.7 reported 1 passing test in 1 test file.
Next.js 16.3.1 production build completed and generated static / and /health routes.

decisions: Kept all application code and configuration under apps/web to preserve the production application and root/shared configuration.
Used Next.js 16.3.1, strict TypeScript, App Router server components, and current audited dependency versions.
Used public environment variables only for labels with safe defaults; secrets are explicitly prohibited from NEXT_PUBLIC variables.
Used Next core-web-vitals lint rules and Vitest with jsdom for the initial unit-test setup.
risks: The shell is deliberately not wired to legacy authentication, APIs, persistence, deployment, or CI orchestration; future migration slices need explicit integration ownership and contracts.
dependencies: Node.js 20.9 or newer is required by Next.js 16.
A separately owned CI change must invoke the documented apps/web commands.
followUps: Add a separately owned CI workflow invocation for apps/web.
Migrate legacy modules only through explicit adapters that preserve existing persistence behavior.
rollback: Revert the LAM-76 commits or remove the unreferenced apps/web directory. No data, schema, API, mapper, localStorage, or production deployment rollback is required.
